name: Marcus Chen
description: I rebuilt my resume in one evening using the live preview. The single-column template read cleanly in our ATS, and I had a polished PDF before my campus career fair.

name: Elena Ruiz
description: Switching careers meant rewriting everything. I saved one profile on Resumes Maker and spun up a second version for logistics roles without retyping ten years of work history.

name: James Okafor
description: Clinical resumes get messy fast. The section order and spacing stayed consistent, and the PDF export looked sharp on hospital HR portals—no weird margins or broken bullets.

name: Rachel Kim
description: I needed a creative layout for agency applications and a tighter one for in-house roles. Same core profile, two templates, two downloads—done in under twenty minutes.

name: Daniel Torres
description: I edited a draft on my phone between client calls. The preview updated instantly, so I knew exactly how the page break would land before I sent the file.

name: Amara Osei
description: No account upsells or watermarks—just pick a template, fill the fields, and download. That alone saved me from juggling another subscription I did not need.

name: Noah Bennett
description: The blog tips on keyword placement helped me tighten my skills section. Combined with an ATS-friendly layout, my resume finally matched how I talk about my work in interviews.

name: Sofia Alvarez
description: I had avoided resume builders for years. This one walked me through experience and education without clutter, and the finished PDF looked professional enough for district postings.

name: Vikram Nair
description: Forty-plus templates sounded overwhelming, but filtering to clean, modern layouts was quick. Export was one click—no waiting on email links or paywalled downloads.

name: Chloe Martin
description: I maintain separate profiles for SaaS and healthcare targets. Updating one bullet propagates everywhere, then I swap templates when a role needs a different emphasis.
